title: Notion says breach at AI vendor Fireworks exposed some AI chat transcripts
excerpt: Notion says fewer than 1% of workspaces were affected after AI provider Fireworks AI was breached, and that the vendor kept data it had agreed not to retain.

sources.title: Notion: Notice about the Fireworks AI incident that may impact some Notion workspaces
The Register: Fireworks AI widens breach disclosure
eSecurity Planet: Fireworks AI Hit by Second Breach: Notion Chat Transcripts Exposed

body_html:
Notion, the US-based workspace and note-taking app, has told customers that some conversations with its built-in AI assistant were exposed in a security incident at one of its suppliers, Fireworks AI, a company that runs AI models for other businesses. Notion says fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces were affected. Fireworks widened its own disclosure on 9 November 2026, and Notion has since published a notice for affected customers.

The case matters beyond one app. Many products people use every day pass their words to outside AI providers behind the scenes. When one of those providers is breached, the people affected may never have heard its name.

What happened, according to the companies

Fireworks AI disclosed two related incidents. According to The Register, the company detected unauthorised use of internal credentials on 6 October 2026, and on 23 and 24 October a third-party cloud provider that hosted its research machines was compromised and used to reach its development systems. In an update on 9 November, Fireworks said billing details, account information and, for certain customers, parts of incomplete AI model weights and datasets had been accessed. It said payment card numbers were not stored and not affected. Fireworks said it worked with an outside forensics team, rotated credentials and isolated affected systems.

Notion's notice to customers says it used Fireworks for a feature called Insights, which helps workspace administrators understand how members use AI, and to run some open-weight models (AI models whose internals are published). In Notion's words: "One of our vendors, Fireworks AI, notified us of a security incident impacting fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces."

According to Notion, the exposed transcripts can include:

  • the full text of what users typed into Notion AI, which may contain names, email addresses, passwords or API keys (digital access passes) if users pasted them in;
  • text selected on the page at the time; and
  • the AI's full replies, which can include fragments of pages the AI referred to.

Notion says most affected transcripts were not linked to a specific user, workspace or company, although outside reporting notes that the text itself can contain identifying details.

A data retention promise

The most significant detail in Notion's notice is about retention. Notion says Fireworks kept data from the services Notion used, even though Fireworks had contractually committed to zero data retention, meaning it should not have stored the content at all. Fireworks' own response to that statement was not included in the sources we reviewed.

What Notion has done

  • Disconnected from Fireworks on 3 November and stopped sending it data. Notion says Fireworks deleted all Notion data on 4 November.
  • Switched off the Insights feature and stopped running open-weight models through Fireworks.
  • Contacted affected customers and added a "Security incident review" tool so workspace owners can download and check the affected data.
  • Announced an audit of its critical vendors to check data minimisation and zero data retention.

Notion advises affected customers to rotate any exposed passwords, keys or tokens, watch for phishing messages that mention the incident, and keep secrets out of chats and documents. Customers who have not been contacted need not take action for now, it says.

What is still unknown

  • How many people's conversations were exposed. Notion gives a share of workspaces, not a number of users.
  • How the cloud provider and the October credentials were first compromised. Fireworks has not said publicly.
  • Whether other Fireworks customers' end users were affected in a similar way. Reports name other customers, but only some have confirmed impact.

Why it matters for staying in charge

People usually agree to share their words with the app in front of them, not with every company behind it. The Private by default Directive (D5) asks that data is kept only as long as needed, and Secure and supported (D6) covers the security of the whole supply chain, not only the product people see. Accountable (D9) asks that someone answers for problems, and that promises such as "zero retention" can be checked.

Incidents like this are why independent standards exist: so that commitments made in contracts can be verified, not only stated. You can ask any maker the questions on our questions to ask page, including which outside providers see your data, and read more on our security page.
